subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: Should `backup create` automatically delete stale OpenClaw-owned backup temp artifacts on startup after a grace window?
rationale: The code blocker is repairable, but the remaining behavior intentionally deletes old partial backup artifacts that operators might otherwise inspect or recover manually.

options.title: Accept guarded startup cleanup
options.body: Land after the matcher covers timestamped and retry temp names, owner checks remain tight, and real terminal proof shows the documented flows are swept safely.

options.title: Accept fixed-output cleanup only
options.body: Allow this PR to cover stable file-output basenames and leave default timestamped archive temps to a follow-up, with the known leak remaining in the main path.

options.title: Pause cleanup policy
options.body: Pause or close if maintainers want recovery/debugging affordances before backup startup deletes stale partial artifacts.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded startup cleanup
recommendation.body: Land after the matcher covers timestamped and retry temp names, owner checks remain tight, and real terminal proof shows the documented flows are swept safely.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to both original backup review context and the extraction of backup creation into the infra owner surface.
